t.2.1.1: The Self-existent pierced the openings of the senses outward; therefore one looks outward and not within the inner self. But a certain wise man, seeking immortality, turned his eyes inward and beheld the Self within.
t.2.1.2: The childish run after outward desires; they walk into the snare of Death that is spread wide. But the wise, having known immortality, do not seek the permanent here among things impermanent.
t.2.1.4: That by which one perceives both the state of dreaming and the state of waking, having known that as the great, all-pervading Self, the wise one does not grieve.
t.2.1.3: That by which one knows form, taste, smell, sounds, and the touches of sexual union, by that very one does one know. What remains here? This, truly, is That.
t.2.1.5: He who knows this honey-eater, the living self, from close at hand, as the lord of what has been and what is to be, no longer shrinks away from it. This, truly, is That.
t.2.1.6: He who sees the one who was born of old from austerity, who came into being before the waters, and who, having entered the cave, abides there and looked forth through the beings, this, truly, is That.
t.2.1.8: Jātavedas, hidden in the two fire-sticks like an embryo well borne by pregnant women, Agni, to be praised day after day by wakeful men bearing oblations: this, truly, is That.
t.2.1.7: She who comes into being with prāṇa, Aditi, made of the deities, who is to be seen abiding in the cave, having entered it, she who was born together with the elements: this, truly, is That.
t.2.1.9: That from which the sun rises and into which it goes to set, in that all the gods are fixed, and no one ever goes beyond it. This, truly, is That.
t.2.1.10: What is here, that indeed is there; what is there, that likewise is here. He goes from death to death who sees here any diversity, as it were.
t.2.1.11: By the mind alone is this to be attained; here there is no diversity whatsoever. He goes from death to death who sees as though there were diversity here.
t.2.1.12: The Puruṣa, the size of a thumb, dwells in the middle of the body, the lord of what has been and what is to be; after knowing him, one no longer shrinks away. This, truly, is That.
t.2.1.13: The Person, the size of a thumb, is like a light without smoke, the lord of what has been and what is to be; he alone is today, and he alone tomorrow. This, truly, is That.
t.2.1.14: As water rained upon a high place runs off in all directions among the mountains, so one who sees the dharmas as separate runs after them alone.
t.2.1.15: As pure water poured into pure water becomes just the same, so, O Gautama, becomes the self of the sage who knows.
